## Summary
- Pin `@zed-industries/codex-acp@0.15.0` as a project-local runtime dependency so `acpx@0.6.1` launches an adapter that advertises GPT-5.5 reasoning variants.
- Normalize Codex GPT-5 `model + reasoning_effort` inputs into ACP model ids like `gpt-5.5/xhigh` before calling acpx.
- Avoid the broken GPT-5.5 flow of `set model gpt-5.5` followed by `set thought_level xhigh`; preserve the legacy separate thought-level path for Claude and unknown/custom Codex models.
- Document the Codex model naming behavior.

## Tests
- `cd .agent && npm test`
- Local smoke: `.agent/node_modules/.bin/acpx --model gpt-5.5/xhigh codex exec ...` selected `codex-acp 0.15.0` and `currentModelId=gpt-5.5/xhigh` before timing out/auth failing.

Stack foundation for superseding #380 and #387.

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 165eeaeceb15033ff0304bb9fc095ff051d45c3a -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

I have everything I need. No existing inline review threads to manage. Let me write the synthesis.

---

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #388 pins `@zed-industries/codex-acp@0.15.0` as a project-local runtime dependency alongside `acpx@0.6.1`, and adds a `resolveAcpxModelSelection` helper that normalizes Codex GPT-5 `model + reasoning_effort` pairs into composed ACP model IDs like `gpt-5.5/xhigh` before invoking acpx. The old two-command sequence (`set model gpt-5.5` → `set thought_level xhigh`) no longer works reliably with the newer adapter; the composed ID form matches what the adapter now advertises. Claude and unknown/custom Codex models keep the legacy separate `thought_level` path. The PR is explicitly scoped as a foundation layer for superseding #380 and #387 — the production `run.ts` wiring that would pass `model` through to `runAcpx` is not included.

## Review

The normalization helper is well-factored, correctly typed, and tested across all three decision branches. The adapter pin is the right strategy. The main concrete concern is that the added documentation paragraph claims present-tense behavior that `run.ts` does not yet support, which could mislead users who configure an `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY` `model` entry and expect composed ACP IDs today.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Docs describe behavior `run.ts` doesn't yet wire | WARNING | The added paragraph states Sepo "accepts…and passes the effective ACP model id to acpx" in present tense, but `run.ts` only passes `thoughtLevel`; the composition is inert in production until `model` is forwarded. |
| `[suffix]` bracket form in `CODEX_REASONING_SUFFIX` undocumented | INFO | The regex accepts `gpt-5.5[xhigh]` and the tests cover it, but neither docs nor a comment explains this encoding, making it look like a dead branch to a future reader. |
| `--model` global flag redundant on named-session prompt calls | INFO | After this PR, `buildAcpxArgs` will emit `--model gpt-5.5/xhigh` on every `codex prompt -s <session>` call for GPT-5 models, in addition to the `set model gpt-5.5/xhigh` command already issued during session setup; worth verifying acpx silently ignores the redundant flag. |

## Progress

- Rubrics review ran and scored PASS (100/100, 9 rubrics), with all surgical-changes, reuse-existing-code, minimal-defaults, and documentation rubrics satisfied.
- The broken transient-session path for GPT-5 exec is fully eliminated: the old `sessions new` → `set model` → `set thought_level` → `set-mode` → `prompt -s <session>` sequence is replaced by a direct `exec --model gpt-5.5/xhigh` with no session.
- Legacy `set thought_level` path for `o3`, Claude, and unknown Codex models is explicitly preserved and covered by retained tests.
- Dependency lockfile includes all six platform optional deps for `@zed-industries/codex-acp@0.15.0`.
- No existing inline review threads to resolve.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Docs describe behavior `run.ts` doesn't yet wire</summary>

**Cause:** The documentation paragraph says "Sepo accepts provider-neutral `model` plus `reasoning_effort` policy entries and passes the effective ACP model id to acpx." In the current codebase, `run.ts` line 514 only passes `thoughtLevel: process.env.MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT` to `runAcpx`; there is no `model:` argument and no `MODEL_ID` env var forwarded through the action. `resolveAcpxModelSelection` short-circuits to the legacy path when `model` is empty, so the composition is never triggered by the production workflow.

**Candidate solutions:**
1. Add a caveat clause to the docs paragraph: "once the `model` action input is wired through, Sepo will…" — keeps the docs honest for the foundation-PR state.
2. Hold the documentation addition for the follow-up PR that also adds `run.ts`/action wiring.
3. Accept the forward-looking present tense as intentional for a foundation PR (author choice).

**Comments:** The PR description explicitly calls this "a stack foundation for superseding #380 and #387", so the gap is intentional. Whether to add a caveat is a product/style call for the author. The rubrics review scored "Write audience-first documentation" as passing without flagging this, which reflects a legitimate authorial choice about tense framing.
</details>

<details>
<summary>`[suffix]` bracket form in `CODEX_REASONING_SUFFIX` undocumented</summary>

**Cause:** `CODEX_REASONING_SUFFIX = /(?:\/(?:low|medium|high|xhigh)|\[(?:low|medium|high|xhigh)\])$/u` accepts both `/`-delimited and `[…]`-delimited effort suffixes. The `[…]` variant is exercised in one test case (`gpt-5.5[xhigh]`) but appears in neither the docs paragraph nor an inline comment.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a one-line comment alongside the constant explaining that `[…]` is a known alternate encoding form (e.g., from an earlier adapter revision), or remove the branch if it is no longer emitted by any real source.
</details>

<details>
<summary>`--model` global flag redundant on named-session prompt calls</summary>

**Cause:** `buildAcpxArgs` already passed `model` as a global flag before this PR. After normalization, GPT-5 Codex named sessions that provide a model will receive both a `set model gpt-5.5/xhigh` setup command and a `--model gpt-5.5/xhigh` global flag on every `prompt -s` call. This pattern was pre-existing for non-composed IDs; the concern is whether the composed form causes any different acpx behavior. The PR smoke test confirmed `currentModelId=gpt-5.5/xhigh` on the exec path, but the named-session path is not tested end-to-end with the new composed ID.

**Candidate solutions:** Verify against acpx docs or source that a redundant global `--model` flag is ignored when a session is active. No code change needed if confirmed harmless.
</details>

## Recommended Next Step

**HUMAN_DECISION** — The one WARNING (docs present-tense framing) is a product/style judgment call for the author in the context of an intentional foundation PR, and both candidate fixes (add caveat vs. defer docs) are equally valid; automated fix-pr should not choose between them without author direction.

## Final Verdict

**MINOR_ISSUES**

## Action Items

- [ ] Decide whether to add a caveat clause to the `configuration-list.md` paragraph ("once `model` is wired through the action input…") or defer the documentation addition to the follow-up PR that completes the `run.ts`/action wiring.
- [ ] Optionally add a brief inline comment to `CODEX_REASONING_SUFFIX` explaining the `[…]` bracket variant, or confirm and remove it if no real adapter emits that form.
